title: Real World VoiceEQ: Measuring the Human Quality of Voice AI
hook: Voice AI benchmarks mostly grade transcripts. Hume AI's new eval says most systems still miss tone, hesitation, and emotion - the parts that make speech sound human.
key_points: Evaluates 4 components - ASR, TTS, speech-to-speech, and speech understanding - across 40+ proprietary and open-source voice models.
Built on 15+ evaluation dimensions and 60+ metrics, grounded in over 1 million human ratings via Hume's 'Kairos' evaluation platform.
No single model ranks in the top five across all capability groups - voice AI is specializing, not converging on one winner.
Many voice models remain fundamentally transcript-driven: they track words spoken but miss tone, pacing, hesitation, emphasis, and volume.
Scores swing sharply with accents, background noise, and emotional speech - gaps transcript-only metrics miss entirely.
content_html: Most voice AI benchmarks grade what a system transcribes, not how it sounds. Hume AI's Real World VoiceEQ tries to close that gap: it evaluates whether voice systems recognize, produce, and respond to tone, emotion, speaker identity, and context - not just words.
extra_html: The benchmark covers four components - automatic speech recognition, text-to-speech, speech-to-speech, and speech understanding - tested across more than 40 leading proprietary and open-source models on 15+ evaluation dimensions and 60+ metrics, grounded in over a million human ratings collected through Hume's Kairos evaluation platform. The headline findings: no model dominates across all capability groups, each specializes differently; most systems remain transcript-driven, tracking words while missing paralinguistic cues like tone and hesitation; scores swing heavily with accents, noise, and emotional speech in ways word-error-rate-style metrics don't capture; and even AI evaluators struggle on subjective judgments where human raters are still hard to replace. Full methodology and leaderboard via the source link.

related.title: Whisper: Robust Speech Recognition at Scale
related.hook: Train a plain encoder-decoder transformer on 680,000 hours of weakly-labeled multilingual audio and you get near-human transcription robustness without task-specific fine-tuning.
